source.title: SharedSAE: One Feature Dictionary Across Language Models
source.authors: D. Ognev; Célian Vasson; Li-Jie Hu; Kentaro Inui; Benjamin Heinzerling

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether sparse SAE features in LLMs can be shared and described across models, while refining the claim that such features form a complete one-concept-per-latent inventory.
record.gate_note: The paper cites superposition as motivation but does not test toy-model superposition, feature sparsity or importance sweeps, or capacity competition. Rows below cover its own LLM SAE reconstruction, cross-model feature alignment, and semantic-transfer results. Cited results and setup-only values are excluded.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a methods paper. SharedSAE's reconstruction and cross-model alignment are its own method's performance, and the alignment is partly enforced by training. Only incidental results bear on V5: observed feature splitting, and limited seed-to-seed matching of dedicated SAEs.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude a shared SAE dictionary is obtainable for their four-model roster. It reconstructs near dedicated ceilings, latents are co-selected with correlated magnitudes, and descriptions transfer. Frozen-dictionary adaptation works. They call functional alignment partial and note feature splitting. They explicitly restrict the claim to the evaluated roster, not to a premise about shared representations.
record.recipe_differences: This study trains shared sparse autoencoders and evaluates cross-model feature alignment in LLMs; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state results vary with aligned-data amount, training budget, and hook layer. The roster uses roughly 85% depth; mid-depth results differ. The paper also reports that a fixed TopK setting can entangle features.

fits_no_version.finding: A jointly trained shared SAE dictionary aligns across four LLM families. Latents are co-selected (58.9/128 vs ~3 chance), magnitudes correlate solo (median 0.785 vs 0.428 post-hoc), and labels and concept detectors transfer. Held-out, instruct, and cross-lab models adapt to the frozen dictionary.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse dictionary features can be made shared across different LLM families (cross-model universality of SAE features).

record.problems: The main roster is four base checkpoints around 1B parameters on English FineWeb-Edu, with hooks at roughly 85% depth; larger-scale models and other languages are untested. Several alignment measures are proxies and some are affected by the shared selection mechanism. FADE transfer results use a clarity-selected subset, and full-coverage automatic labeling remains unresolved. Functional evidence is explicitly partial.
record.rows_left_out: Other reconstruction and splice metrics, ablation results, additional baseline comparisons, adaptation reconstruction ratios, detailed label-score columns, and appendix diagnostics were omitted because they do not add a distinct result needed for the tested versions within the row limit.

untested.parts: No toy-model superposition. The planted-concept synthetic check (Appendix J) validates the method; it does not test sparsity-dependent transitions or geometry.
Capacity competition and dedicated dimensions for important features are not examined.
Alternative causes of polysemanticity are not examined.
No measure of feature spread across neurons. SAE reconstruction FVE is reported only as method performance (raw-dimension matching floor 0.14 is a control).
Completeness is not tested. Canonicality across dictionary sizes is not tested. Stability is assessed only via one Qwen3 seed pair of dedicated SAEs.
No comparison of 1-D vs multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: Seed stability of dedicated SAEs. Two converged Qwen3 SAEs from different seeds match at median 0.770 best-match and 0.871 mutual-best. The cross-model post-hoc median is 0.450.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4/V5 'supports' labels were dropped. Those rows measure the authors' method, whose cross-model sharing is enforced by training and evaluated against competing methods, so they do not test whether LLMs contain sparse features or whether SAE features are canonical units. The sharing finding is moved to fits_no_version. V5 rests on thin evidence: one splitting anecdote at an earlier protocol, plus a single-seed-pair control.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, more sparse features than dimensions, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or important features receiving dedicated dimensions.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity indicates superposition.
The study evaluates SAE-recovered features in LLMs, but does not measure feature spread across neurons or compare SAE features with neuron-level representations.
It evaluates semantic transfer and reports feature splitting, but does not establish completeness, canonicality, or stability across arbitrary training runs and model populations.
No comparison of one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: SharedSAE on four-model roster
rows.operation_detail: Compared each model's solo top-128 latent selections on aligned tokens.
rows.measure: Mean number of latents selected by all four models per token
rows.baseline: Chance level is about 3 of 128; matched dedicated SAEs: 13.5 of 128
rows.note: The value is an aggregate over the four-model roster.
rows.check: Selection agreement of a dictionary trained to share latents. Partly by construction (authors concede this); it measures method performance against baselines.

rows.subject: SharedSAE on four-model roster
rows.operation_detail: Correlated sparse-code magnitudes across model pairs for each shared latent under solo inference.
rows.note: The paper reports 86% of measured SharedSAE latents above 0.5 correlation.
rows.check: Cross-model correlation of a jointly trained dictionary; the baseline is a competing method. Does not test whether SAE features are canonical model units.

rows.subject: SharedSAE shared-vote labels
rows.operation_detail: Reported the fraction of shared-vote labels retained after the cross-stream clarity protocol.

conditions.value: clarity at least 0.9 in at least one stream

rows.note: The authors caution that these results concern a clarity-filtered subset, not full-coverage labeling.
rows.check: Retained coverage is a property of the labeling protocol (authors say so), not of feature completeness.

rows.operation_detail: Compared decoded top-activating tokens and token sets across model pairs.
rows.note: This is a token-level proxy for shared feature meaning.

rows.subject: SharedSAE
rows.operation_detail: Compared decoded top-activating token sets across model pairs.
rows.note: This is a token-level proxy for shared feature meaning.

rows.subject: SharedSAE
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated cross-model average-precision retention for selected concept detectors.

conditions.value: five most selective per model across ten concept categories

rows.note: The per-category SharedSAE retentions range from 0.990 to 1.000.

rows.subject: SharedSAE
rows.operation_detail: Reported two separate latents with activating examples labelled as United.
rows.value: Two separate United detectors; authors state the dictionary is not a one-concept-per-latent inventory.
rows.note: The authors say latent counts can overstate concept counts.
rows.check: Single qualitative instance (two 'United' latents), measured at an earlier protocol (Table 15). Authors generalise: the dictionary is not a one-concept-per-latent inventory.

rows.subject: SharedSAE candidate latents
rows.operation_detail: Compared the same latent's top-30 causally promoted token strings across models.
rows.measure: Median cross-model overlap of causally promoted tokens
rows.note: The authors call string overlap a lower bound and describe functional alignment as partial.
rows.check: Causal-effect agreement of the shared dictionary across models; this is method alignment, not V5.

rows.subject: SharedSAE adapted models
rows.stage_stated: adapted; Llama checkpoint is post-trained, others not stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared adapted models' solo-code feature activations with seed-model activations on six probe-found latents.
rows.note: Top-50 position overlaps reach 44 of 50; the correlation range is reported across adapted models and features.
rows.check: Adaptation performance of the method on six hand-selected latents. The 0.64–0.99 range is pooled over models and latents.

relationships.condition: Late-depth (~85%) SAEs on four ~1B base LLMs
relationships.reason: Feature splitting observed: 'United' appears as two latents (R13). Two dedicated Qwen3 SAEs from different seeds match only at median 0.770 best-match correlation (text, App. D.3; not in rows). So latents are neither one-concept-per-latent nor fully seed-stable.
relationships.display_finding: 'United' appeared as two latents, and two dedicated Qwen3 SAEs from different seeds matched only at a median best-match correlation of 0.770, so latents were neither one concept each nor fully seed-stable.
